Let \(R(t)\) be the remaining resource stock at time \(t\), and let \(r\) be the instantaneous depletion rate proportional to the current stock (\(dR/dt = -rR\)). The solution is \(R(t) = R_0 e^{-rt}\). The doubling time of the abandonment rate implies \(r\) itself grows exponentially, leading to a singularity where \(R ightarrow 0\) in finite time. This mirrors the GSI concept of 'betting line shocks'—when a critical threshold of information (e.g., injury reports) triggers a cascade of bets, depleting liquidity at an accelerating pace until the market freezes.
